title: RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring
summary: Real-world video deblurring remains challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and the scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream pipelines such as mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction. This work presents \textbf{RealVDeblur}, an efficient generative framework designed to improve in-the-wild robustness under diverse real capture conditions. First, a large-scale, physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline is constructed from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos, providing realistic training data covering both camera-induced and object-motion blur. Second, a video diffusion prior is leveraged for restoration; to better accommodate frame-dependent blur variations, temporal compression in the VAE is disabled and a frame-wise encoding scheme is adopted. For practical deployment on long videos, multi-step diffusion sampling is distilled into an efficient one-step generator, and a training-free Temporal Window Mask stabilizes inference beyond the training horizon with constant memory usage. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, as well as improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur. Project page: https://rbjin.github.io/RealVDeblur

AI.tldr: RealVDeblur is an efficient generative framework for real-world video deblurring that uses a physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline from 3DGS assets and high-frame-rate videos, leverages video diffusion prior with frame-wise VAE encoding, distills multi-step diffusion into one-step generation, and employs a Temporal Window Mask for stable long-video inference, demonstrating strong performance across diverse benchmarks and downstream 3D reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Real-world video deblurring is challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream tasks like mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction.
AI.method: (1) A large-scale physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline using scene-level 3DGS assets and high-frame-rate videos; (2) Video diffusion prior with disabled temporal VAE compression and frame-wise encoding for blur variations; (3) Distillation of multi-step diffusion into a one-step generator; (4) Training-free Temporal Window Mask for stable long-video inference.
AI.result: Strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, plus improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur.
AI.conclusion: RealVDeblur effectively addresses real-world video deblurring with robust in-the-wild performance and practical efficiency for long videos and downstream applications.

title: Masked Topology Modeling for Self-Supervised Learning on Parametric CAD
summary:
Computer aided design (CAD) is ubiquitous: virtually any modern object was designed using editable CAD tools. However, with the shortage of available CAD datasets in its native editable and parametric format, boundary representation (B-Rep), it is ever more important to develop data-efficient methods for this domain.
  We present a new self-supervised pretraining task, Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), that leverages the face-adjacency graph, an induced structure unique to B-reps that the encoder can be asked to reconstruct. MTM masks a fraction of edges and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from the encoder's post-message-passing face features.
  We combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations, a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective, and pretraining on the ABC dataset and our new procedurally generated dataset to show strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), a self-supervised pretraining method for CAD boundary representation (B-Rep) data that masks edges in face-adjacency graphs and predicts their convexity/curve type, combined with contrastive learning and masked-reconstruction objectives.
AI.motivation: The shortage of available CAD datasets in native editable and parametric format (B-Rep) necessitates data-efficient methods for this domain.
AI.method: MTM masks a fraction of edges in face-adjacency graphs and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from encoder's post-message-passing face features. Combined with MoCo-style contrastive learning over B-Rep-aware augmentations and BFS-connected face-region masked reconstruction.
AI.result: Strong performance demonstrated on a number of benchmarks after pretraining on ABC dataset and a new procedurally generated dataset.
AI.conclusion: Self-supervised pretraining via MTM and contrastive learning is effective for B-Rep CAD data, addressing data scarcity issues.

title: Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion
summary: Recent 3D generative models produce high-quality geometry from a single image using large-scale priors and diffusion architectures. However, they assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Although prior works address these challenges individually, they lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals. We present Axolotl3D, a multi-modal and occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor promoting faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data, enabling robust cross-modal reasoning. Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, as well as strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

AI.tldr: Axolotl3D is a multi-modal, occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and partial point clouds to enable controllable 3D completion under diverse inputs, achieving state-of-the-art results on Toys4K and OmniObject3D.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D generative models assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Prior works address these challenges individually but lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals.
AI.method: Axolotl3D jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud acts as a geometric anchor for faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance on Toys4K and OmniObject3D under both clean and occluded settings, plus strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.
AI.conclusion: Axolotl3D provides a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals, outperforming prior works in multi-view, occluded, and editing scenarios.

title: ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs
summary: Modeling continuous object deformation is important for many computer vision and robotics tasks, such as manipulation and simulation. Existing approaches rely on learning-based methods or physics simulators to model shape deformations. However, these approaches either use discrete time steps or are too computationally intensive for real-time applications. We present ODeform, a novel extension of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space. Our method transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions (like material properties) into a unified latent space. By solving the resulting ordinary differential equations over time, we model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating the need for discrete time steps while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on unseen physical parameter configurations, showing improved motion prediction accuracy over baseline methods. Our experiments further demonstrate a successful transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes, along with effective interpolation and extrapolation of the learned dynamics. Our code and data will be made publicly available.

AI.tldr: ODeform extends Neural ODEs to model continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space, achieving efficient and accurate deformation prediction without discrete time steps.
AI.motivation: Existing deformation modeling methods rely on discrete time steps or are computationally intensive, limiting real-time applications. There is a need for continuous, efficient deformation modeling for computer vision and robotics tasks.
AI.method: ODeform transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions into a unified latent space, then solves ODEs over time to model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating discrete time steps while maintaining efficiency.
AI.result: Outperforms baseline methods on unseen physical parameter configurations; successfully transfers to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes; demonstrates effective interpolation and extrapolation of learned dynamics.
AI.conclusion: ODeform provides a computationally efficient, continuous approach to deformable object modeling that generalizes well to unseen configurations and real-world objects.

title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
comment: Accepted to the Workshop on Data Quality Aware, High-Performance, and Trustworthy AI Systems for Healthcare at IEEE/ACM CHASE 2026
summary: Concept Bottleneck Models provide interpretable-by-design predictions by mediating diagnosis through human-understandable concepts, but in medical imaging, their trustworthiness is often limited by the quality and granularity of available supervision. In particular, predicted concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, leading to spatially unfaithful explanations. We study a data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) that leverages coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to encourage anatomically plausible concept evidence. For breast ultrasound, we derive two clinically motivated zones from each lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion region of interest for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. We train concept maps using a grouped spatial grounding objective and preserve semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the proposed SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. We also perform a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to quantify the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness. Overall, the results underscore the need for data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation for deployable healthcare AI systems.

AI.tldr: SG-CBM improves interpretable breast ultrasound diagnosis by using coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to spatially ground concept activations, enhancing both diagnostic accuracy and spatial faithfulness of concept evidence.
AI.motivation: Concept Bottleneck Models in medical imaging suffer from spatially unfaithful explanations where predicted concept activations are driven by irrelevant regions, limiting trustworthiness due to quality and granularity of available supervision.
AI.method: Proposes SG-CBM with (i) two clinically motivated zones from lesion masks (in-lesion for morphology, posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena), (ii) grouped spatial grounding objective for training concept maps, (iii) linear bottleneck classifier for semantic faithfulness, and (iv) Train-corrupt/Test-clean stress test for annotation quality impact assessment.
AI.result: Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, SG-CBM improved diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence.
AI.conclusion: Data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation are essential for deployable healthcare AI systems.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation
summary: We present a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge. The approach combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline that filters generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning. Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off, with the best-performing model achieving a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and competitive visual fidelity with an FID of 0.3290. While the proposed geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, highlighting an important frontier for future privacy-preserving medical image generation.

AI.tldr: A privacy-preserving synthetic lung CT generation framework combining Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with a geometric Supervisor filtering pipeline, achieving PPS 0.549 and FID 0.3290, but still vulnerable to patient re-identification.
AI.motivation: To generate realistic synthetic lung CT slices while preserving patient privacy, addressing the challenge that preventing direct image copying may not be sufficient to remove deeper anatomical identity.
AI.method: Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching + privacy-oriented training + post-generation Supervisor pipeline using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning.
AI.result: Best model achieves Privacy Preservation Score 0.549 and FID 0.3290. Geometric filtering reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage.
AI.conclusion: Current methods can mitigate direct copying but fail to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, pointing to a key frontier for future medical image generation privacy.

title: U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation
summary: Interactive image segmentation is critical for efficient image annotation; however, existing methods often require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly. We propose Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR), a novel inference-time framework that enables models to autonomously self-correct after each user interaction. U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to guide the placement of internal pseudo-clicks. These self-generated clicks target the most ambiguous boundary regions, providing strong corrective signals without additional manual input. To support this process, we design a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder backbone: a segmentation head ensures region consistency, while an edge head sharpens boundary alignment. In inference, U-CFR launches a cascade of refinement steps, where each stage leverages the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to refine the mask progressively. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed U-CFR improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy. It reduces the required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley and offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

AI.tldr: U-CFR is an inference-time framework that lets interactive segmentation models self-correct after each user click by generating internal pseudo-clicks guided by a boundary-aware uncertainty score, reducing the number of required manual clicks.
AI.motivation: Existing interactive segmentation methods need too many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement that converges slowly, making annotation inefficient.
AI.method: U-CFR uses a boundary-aware uncertainty score (fusing segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and edge predictions) to guide internal pseudo-clicks; a dual-head network (segmentation + edge heads) is used, and during inference a cascade of refinement steps is performed.
AI.result: U-CFR reduces required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley, and improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy.
AI.conclusion: U-CFR offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation pipeline by enabling autonomous self-correction without extra manual input.

title: Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness
summary: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) is expected to detect events that match a user-specified definition of abnormality. This requirement is stronger than generic anomaly localization: in the same video, changing the definition should change which temporal regions are scored as anomalous. We show that current OWVAD evaluation largely fails to isolate this conditional behavior. Standard VAD metrics and the dynamic-definition protocol can be dominated by target-versus-normal separation, allowing models to obtain strong scores while remaining nearly insensitive to the queried definition. We call this failure mode definition blindness. To explain why it is missed, we decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination, and find that the former receives 7.2-26.8$\times$ more weight across common VAD benchmarks. Motivated by this diagnosis, we introduce three definition-conditioned evaluation metrics, DC-Disc, DC-Det$Δ$, and DC-Sel$Δ$, which progressively remove normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection shortcuts. Experiments on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD reveal that several strong VAD, OWVAD, and general vision language model baselines localize anomalous moments but exhibit weak definition following, often with near-zero definition-response margins. To validate that the failure is actionable, we further introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC points on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 points on DC-Det$Δ$. Overall, our results argue that OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

AI.tldr: Current OWVAD evaluations suffer from "definition blindness," where models detect anomalies without following user-specific definitions. The authors propose new metrics and a definition-contrastive scoring method (DeCoS) to address this.
AI.motivation: Existing OWVAD evaluations fail to isolate whether models truly respond to user-specified definitions of abnormality vs. simply detecting generic anomalies.
AI.method: The authors decompose dynamic-definition evaluation, introduce three definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ), and propose DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule.
AI.result: Strong baselines show weak definition-following; DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 on DC-DetΔ.
AI.conclusion: OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

title: 3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch
summary: Recent advances in 3D scene editing have leveraged iterative diffusion models to update input views. However, this process is computationally expensive and struggles to produce sharp details. Meanwhile, ``hallucination drift'' frequently introduces multi-view inconsistencies, leading to structural artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints. To address this problem, we present 3D-GIMP (3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets Patch Matching), a novel hybrid paradigm designed for high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of diffusing every view, 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, which serves as an appearance prior. We then introduce a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate these reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, effectively bypassing the stochastic nature of frame-by-frame diffusion. By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP maintains high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions while ensuring a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction. Our experiments demonstrate that 3D-GIMP not only achieves competitive inpainting quality as previous methods using diffusion in multiple views, but also outperforms these methods in rendering speed and view consistency.

AI.tldr: 3D-GIMP introduces a hybrid paradigm for object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting that uses a single generative inpainting on a key reference view combined with a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate textures across views, avoiding computationally expensive iterative diffusion per view and achieving faster rendering with better view consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D scene editing methods using iterative diffusion models are computationally expensive, struggle with sharp details, and suffer from "hallucination drift" causing multi-view inconsistencies and structural artifacts during novel view rendering.
AI.method: 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view as an appearance prior, then uses a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm for correspondence matching to propagate reference textures across all remaining views, bypassing frame-by-frame diffusion.
AI.result: 3D-GIMP achieves competitive inpainting quality compared to multi-view diffusion methods while outperforming them in rendering speed and view consistency, maintaining high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions.
AI.conclusion: By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP provides a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction that is both faster and more view-consistent than previous diffusion-based approaches for object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting.

title: Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality
summary: Virtual reality (VR) headsets (e.g., Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro) provide a seamless user experience due to their fast, frictionless interaction with the physical world in a simulated environment. User authentication relies on biometric cues such as iris in such headsets. However, traditional iris recognition protocols may not be adequate in cases of unconstrained acquisition, which is typical of VR-based data. In this work, we examine three crucial aspects: (1) evaluating ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset and analyzing their limitations, (2) addressing data-specific challenges such as off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection using generative models, and (3) performing unimodal (iris, periocular) recognition and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular). We observe that some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; whereas, image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition performance. We will release the evaluation scripts upon acceptance for reproducibility.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates ISO/IEC iris quality metrics on VR headset data, addresses VR-specific challenges (off-axis gaze, illumination, reflections) using generative models, and demonstrates that multimodal fusion (iris + periocular) improves recognition accuracy by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition.
AI.motivation: Traditional iris recognition protocols may fail under unconstrained acquisition conditions typical of VR headsets, necessitating a re-evaluation of standard quality metrics and development of tailored solutions.
AI.method: (1) Evaluate ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on the VRBiom dataset; (2) Use generative models to address VR-specific challenges like off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection; (3) Perform unimodal (iris, periocular) and multimodal score-level fusion recognition.
AI.result: Margin adequacy metric fails on VR-acquired data; image adjustments benefit periocular recognition more; multimodal fusion reduces EER by ~11% compared to unimodal iris recognition.
AI.conclusion: Standard iris quality metrics are inadequate for VR-acquired biometric data, and multimodal fusion significantly improves performance, highlighting the need for VR-specific biometric authentication protocols.

title: SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization
summary: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting enables efficient and generalizable novel-view synthesis. However, high-resolution rendering faces a critical trade-off where increasing input resolution improves detail at the expense of quadratically rising network computational cost. Conversely, maintaining low-resolution inputs stabilizes this cost but results in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. To address this, we propose SubSplat, which introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer(SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density directly from low-resolution features. We further enhance the reparameterization quality through feature aggregation, which effectively captures high-frequency details across multiple views. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency. Our results validate that the proposed framework successfully resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting.

AI.tldr: SubSplat introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, enabling high-fidelity novel-view synthesis from low-resolution inputs without quadratic computational cost increases.
AI.motivation: Existing pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting faces a trade-off: high-resolution inputs improve detail but cause quadratically rising network costs, while low-resolution inputs are efficient but result in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts.
AI.method: SubSplat proposes (1) Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density from low-resolution features; (2) feature aggregation to enhance reparameterization quality by capturing high-frequency details across multiple views.
AI.result: Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency, successfully resolving the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and computational cost.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SubSplat framework effectively resolves the inherent trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost.

title: Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units
comment: Accepted at the 14th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII 2026)
summary: Stress is a dynamic process characterized by significant individual variability in facial expression. Traditional architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often overlook person-specific baselines or lack the representational capacity to model the non-linear temporal progression of distress due to sequential bottlenecks and rigid grid-based constraints. Furthermore, many deep learning models lack the interpretability required for clinical deployment. This study introduces StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages the relational inductive bias of graph modeling to capture complex facial dynamics that indicate acute stress. By using Differential Action Units, the framework normalizes individual responses relative to neutral baselines to achieve personalized recognition. The proposed model achieves 88.62\% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort (58 participants) using a subject-independent, Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation protocol. Beyond predictive accuracy, the architecture integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal distinct expressivity phenotypes. By simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability, this framework provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring.

AI.tldr: StressGAT introduces a Graph Attention Network with Differential Action Units and MIL attention to achieve 88.62% accuracy in personalized stress recognition while providing interpretability through identified peak stress intervals and expressivity phenotypes.
AI.motivation: Traditional RNN/CNN architectures overlook person-specific baselines, lack capacity for non-linear temporal distress modeling, and suffer from poor interpretability for clinical deployment.
AI.method: Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Differential Action Units for personalized normalization relative to neutral baselines, integrated with Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism for interpretability.
AI.result: 88.62% accuracy on a 58-participant stress-induction cohort using subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation.
AI.conclusion: StressGAT provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring by simultaneously optimizing accuracy and interpretability.

title: Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation
summary: Generating realistic interior furniture layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints (e.g., walls, doors, and windows) remains a fundamental challenge in automated spatial design. Existing approaches, primarily based on one-shot generation using diffusion models or Large Language Models (LLMs), lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, often resulting in structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints. To address these challenges, we propose Agentic Designer, a progressive, multi-agent framework that formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative and constraint-verified decision process. By decomposing layout synthesis into modular stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, the framework coordinates three specialized agents, a Generator, an Evaluator, and a Refiner, through a Progressive Consensus Mechanism. This mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, thereby preventing error accumulation. To facilitate this structure-aware paradigm and standardize evaluation, we establish InStruct, a comprehensive benchmark that integrates a dataset comprising over 18,000 high-quality, parametrically annotated samples with a novel suite of structure-centric metrics. Extensive quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies show that Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

AI.tldr: Agentic Designer is a multi-agent framework that generates realistic interior furniture layouts through iterative proposal, verification, and refinement stages, outperforming existing methods on strict structural adherence and functional coherence.
AI.motivation: Existing one-shot generation methods (diffusion models, LLMs) for interior layout design lack intermediate geometric constraint verification, leading to structural collisions and infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints.
AI.method: Proposes a progressive multi-agent framework (Generator, Evaluator, Refiner) with a Progressive Consensus Mechanism that decomposes layout synthesis into iterative stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, enforcing stepwise geometric validation before each placement. Also introduces the InStruct benchmark with 18,000+ parametrically annotated samples and structure-centric metrics.
AI.result: Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies, showing substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.
AI.conclusion: The progressive, constraint-verified multi-agent approach effectively prevents error accumulation and produces structurally valid interior layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints such as walls, doors, and windows.

title: ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse expert-level tasks, but they still struggle with fundamental abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous observation of the real world, such as spatial perception and dynamic reasoning. Recent studies have recognized this gap and introduced dedicated benchmarks to evaluate the spatial-temporal capabilities of MLLMs. However, existing benchmarks mostly focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues largely underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Visual Spatial-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark (ViSTR-Bench), a novel evaluation suite designed to systematically assess whether MLLMs can perform qualitative reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes. Guided by the principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation, ViSTR-Bench establishes a comprehensive four-dimensional evaluations covering Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics. The benchmark comprises 15 distinct subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video question-answer pairs spanning diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios. Extensive evaluations of a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs reveal that, despite their strong general video understanding capabilities, current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces ViSTR-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate whether MLLMs can perform qualitative spatial-temporal reasoning from continuous video cues across motion perception, spatial relations, outcome prediction, and physical dynamics. Current models still fall far below human performance.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive qualitative reasoning from temporal cues in dynamic scenes largely underexplored.
AI.method: ViSTR-Bench is designed with three guiding principles (temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, qualitative evaluation) and comprises 15 subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video QA pairs covering tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios across four dimensions: Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs show that current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.
AI.conclusion: Despite strong general video understanding capabilities, current MLLMs lack fundamental spatial-temporal reasoning abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous real-world observation.

title: Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning
summary: Training deep learning models with freely available web images can reduce their dependence on costly manual annotations. Although webly supervised learning has been widely studied for single-label recognition, its multi-label counterpart remains underexplored, partly due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols. To address this gap, we construct a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR), including Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting. The two datasets cover the same 80 and 20 categories as MS-COCO and Pascal VOC, respectively, and contain about 300 thousand images retrieved from the Internet using category-word combinations as search keywords. We further propose a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework, which learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations together with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels. Extensive experiments on the benchmark demonstrate that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR) with two datasets (Web-COCO, Web-Pascal) and proposes DBMLCL, a dual-branch contrastive learning framework that effectively handles noisy web labels by learning instance-level and category-level representations.
AI.motivation: Webly supervised learning for multi-label recognition is underexplored due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols, despite its potential to reduce reliance on costly manual annotations.
AI.method: The authors construct Web-COCO and Web-Pascal benchmarks (300K web images) and propose DBMLCL, a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning framework that learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations along with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels.
AI.result: DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines on the proposed WS-MLR benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark and DBMLCL framework advance webly supervised multi-label recognition, providing a unified evaluation protocol and an effective noise-handling approach.

title: WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing
summary: Recent one-step text-to-image (T2I) models enable efficient image synthesis and provide new opportunities for real-time image editing. However, existing one-step editing methods primarily rely on text conditioning for semantic transformation, lacking explicit spatial control over \textit{where} to edit. More importantly, even when spatial constraints are introduced, these methods often struggle to achieve strong and stable semantic modifications within the target regions. In this work, we revisit one-step image editing from a spatially controlled perspective and identify two key challenges: discovering editable regions and achieving effective localized semantic transformation. We reveal that existing methods perform global semantic transport, which limits high-intensity local editing under the one-step setting. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{WhereEdit}, a framework that reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing. WhereEdit automatically identifies semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency. Experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark demonstrate that WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining the efficiency of one-step generation. Additional experiments with region-level supervision further highlight the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step image editing.

AI.tldr: WhereEdit is a framework for one-step text-to-image editing that automatically identifies editable regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation, enabling strong localized semantic edits while preserving non-target regions and structural consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing one-step image editing methods lack explicit spatial control over where to edit and struggle to achieve strong, stable semantic modifications within target regions under the one-step setting.
AI.method: WhereEdit reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing by: (1) automatically identifying semantically relevant regions from internal model features, and (2) applying adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency.
AI.result: Experiments on PIE-Bench benchmark show WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining one-step generation efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Explicit spatial reasoning is crucial for high-quality one-step image editing, and WhereEdit's localized adaptive approach effectively addresses the limitations of global semantic transport methods.

title: Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting
summary: Editable 3D scene creation requires object instances and lights that can be inspected, moved, and imported into standard engines, yet existing single-image methods largely stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation. We introduce Lumera (Light-aware Unified Engine-native Reconstruction and Assembly), a benchmark and reference pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing from a single image. Lumera-2K is built from 2,513 UE5 projects and provides 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views. On this data, Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I), which are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. In a sanitized box benchmark against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D, Lumera-Box obtains the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762), while WildDet3D remains stronger on anchor recall. For lights, Lumera-Light recovers almost all non-empty scenes (recall 0.998) but remains limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, and intensity Pearson r=0.628. These results establish parametric lights as a measurable editable-scene target and expose remaining bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

AI.tldr: Lumera introduces a benchmark and reference pipeline (Lumera-2K dataset, Lumera-Box, Lumera-Light) for parsing engine-native, light-aware 3D scenes from a single image, enabling editable scene reconstruction with parametric lights and object instances.
AI.motivation: Existing single-image 3D methods stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation, lacking the ability to produce editable 3D scenes with inspectable, movable object instances and lights compatible with standard engines.
AI.method: Builds Lumera-2K dataset (2,513 UE5 projects, 63M object instances, 102.6K parametric lights). Adapts VLM to parse object boxes (Lumera-Box) and parametric light tuples (Lumera-Light), then assembles with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop.
AI.result: Lumera-Box achieves best overall detection/geometry/semantic/layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762). Lumera-Light recovers 0.998 recall for non-empty scenes but limited individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5m); matched lights show median pos error 0.261m, ΔE2000 4.59, intensity Pearson r=0.628.
AI.conclusion: Parametric lights are established as a measurable editable-scene target. Remaining bottlenecks include relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

title: MAGE-Vein: Multi-Instance Age and Gender Estimation from Finger Vein Images
summary: Age estimation from finger vein images has been widely considered impractical due to severe demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors like gender. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE-Vein, a novel multi-instance, multi-task learning framework. Our approach extracts robust structural aging signs by employing a hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers, effectively suppressing local imaging noise. Furthermore, simultaneous optimization of gender classification conditions the network to effectively eliminate gender-specific vascular variations. Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880. Our results not only overturn the conventional consensus regarding the limitations of the finger vein modality but also demonstrate that previous estimation failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsisaoki/MAGE-Vein.

AI.tldr: MAGE-Vein is a multi-instance, multi-task learning framework for age estimation from finger vein images that achieves MAE of 6.12 years by using three-finger fusion and gender conditioning, overturning prior beliefs that this modality was impractical due to dataset biases.
AI.motivation: Age estimation from finger vein images was previously considered impractical due to demographic biases in public datasets and confounding physiological factors (e.g., gender). The paper aims to overturn this conventional consensus.
AI.method: A multi-instance, multi-task learning framework (MAGE-Vein) that uses hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers to suppress local imaging noise, and simultaneous gender classification optimization to eliminate gender-specific vascular variations.
AI.result: On a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880.
AI.conclusion: The results overturn the conventional consensus that finger vein images are impractical for age estimation, demonstrating that previous failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets.

title: DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing
summary: With the increasing diversity of spoofing attacks, there is a growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. While existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate high generalization in this context, they heavily rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. In this paper, we propose DINO-VPT, a lightweight, vision-only framework leveraging hierarchical visual prompt tuning. By dynamically injecting prompts conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), our method effectively disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without requiring multimodal fusion. Evaluations on the UniAttackData benchmark demonstrate that DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. Our results indicate that a properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without the need for multimodal supervision.

AI.tldr: DINO-VPT is a lightweight, vision-only Face Anti-Spoofing framework using hierarchical visual prompt tuning with a Prompt Routing Network, achieving state-of-the-art performance on unified FAS without requiring multimodal fusion.
AI.motivation: To address the growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing models capable of detecting both physical and digital spoofing attacks, while reducing reliance on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders used in existing VLM-based approaches.
AI.method: Proposes DINO-VPT, a vision-only framework that uses hierarchical visual prompt tuning with a Prompt Routing Network (PRN) to dynamically inject prompts conditioned on input features, disentangling diverse spoofing artifacts without multimodal fusion.
AI.result: Achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods on the UniAttackData benchmark.
AI.conclusion: A properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without needing multimodal supervision.

title: Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos
comment: 35 pages, 18 figures. Under review at Scientific Reports
summary: We examine whether richer visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube segmented into over 50,000 ten-second clips and represented across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Spearman correlation analysis reveals the expected ordering along the temporal-richness continuum, with video features showing the strongest continuous alignment. However, this ordering breaks down under binary classification of high- versus low-engagement moments (the paradigm most commonly used to train perceptual scoring models), where TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. An independent two-alternative forced-choice study on Amazon Mechanical Turk confirms that this parity reflects human judgment: participants identified engaging moments with comparable accuracy from TAIs and full video clips, while text performed substantially worse and audio remained near chance. Gap analysis reveals a functional dissociation: video features are advantaged in activity-driven scenes with dynamic content, whereas TAIs better align with human judgments in composition-driven scenes dominated by stable spatial structure. These findings challenge the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned, and suggest that perceptually grounded temporal compression can be a principled alternative to full video encoding.

AI.tldr: Richer visual representations (video) align better with human engagement judgments in continuous ranking, but under binary classification (high vs. low engagement), temporally averaged images (TAIs) match or outperform video. Human studies confirm this parity, with video excelling in dynamic/activity-driven scenes and TAIs in static/composition-driven scenes.
AI.motivation: To examine whether richer visual representations (e.g., full video) yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement compared to simpler representations like TAIs, challenging the assumption that more temporal richness is inherently better.
AI.method: Analyzed 61 first-person city-walk videos (50,000+ 10-second clips) across four modalities: video features, TAIs, audio embeddings, and text descriptions. Used Spearman correlation for continuous alignment, binary classification for high/low engagement, and a two-alternative forced-choice study on MTurk.
AI.result: Video features best align with human judgments in continuous ranking; but in binary classification, TAIs match or outperform video. Human study confirms TAIs and video yield comparable accuracy; text is worse, audio near chance. Video excels in dynamic scenes; TAIs excel in static, composition-driven scenes.
AI.conclusion: Richer representations are not always more human-aligned; perceptually grounded temporal compression (TAIs) can be a principled alternative to full video encoding for engagement assessment.

title: FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head
summary: We propose FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery. The core of our method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches. Our analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation. To address the first issue, we introduce a symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy that leverages the inherent semantics and structural symmetry of human heads. To disentangle the objectives of reconstruction and animation, we develop a novel dual-phase training pipeline that separates the model's capabilities for large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. Moreover, we enhance our model to support multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction in an efficient and memory-friendly manner through a core autoregressive modification with tailored visibility-aware token fusion. Collectively, these innovations enable FA-LAM to reconstruct animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, particularly in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

AI.tldr: FA-LAM is a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model that creates animatable 3D/4D Gaussian heads from a single photo, solving attention noise and reconstruction-animation conflicts via symmetric semantic regularization and a dual-phase training pipeline.
AI.motivation: Existing one-shot animatable head models suffer from low-quality 3D full-head generation due to (1) incorrect/noisy attention activations and (2) conflicts between reconstruction and animation tasks in the training pipeline.
AI.method: (1) Symmetric and semantic attention regularization to enforce correct attention patterns using head structure priors. (2) A dual-phase training pipeline that separates large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. (3) Core autoregressive modification with visibility-aware token fusion for efficient multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction.
AI.result: FA-LAM achieves superior quality in animatable Gaussian full-head reconstruction, especially in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.
AI.conclusion: By disentangling reconstruction and animation objectives and regularizing attention mechanisms, FA-LAM significantly improves one-shot animatable head generation quality and extends to efficient 4D reconstruction.

title: MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer
summary: Makeup-transfer applies the reference makeup to the source face while preserving the source identity. Despite advances in full-face editing by diffusion-based methods, strong regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation remain challenging. The reasons are (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment that causes spillover into non-target areas and weakens regional control; (ii) unclear transfer/preservation concept separation under two-image conditioning, leading to coupling between makeup attributes and identity; and (iii) the lack of a high-resolution dataset that is identity-consistent and region-labeled for fine-grained supervision. In this paper, we propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable and high-fidelity makeup transfer, built on spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. To enable precise region-specific editing while preserving identity, we propose Token-Aligned Region Gating, which aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating. To clarify the concepts of transfer and preservation, we further introduce Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, which aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception. We also design a pipeline for the generation of 1024 x 1024 data pairs through region-specific makeup removal and establish a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MagicMakeup improves regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

AI.tldr: MagicMakeup is a diffusion transformer framework for region-controllable, high-fidelity makeup transfer that uses Token-Aligned Region Gating and Cross-Modal Perception Guidance to solve pixel-to-attention misalignment and concept coupling, achieving superior results across styles, races, and poses.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based makeup transfer methods struggle with (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment causing spillover into non-target areas, (ii) unclear separation between transfer and preservation concepts under two-image conditioning, and (iii) lack of high-resolution identity-consistent region-labeled datasets for fine-grained supervision.
AI.method: MagicMakeup proposes three key contributions: (1) Token-Aligned Region Gating that aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating for precise regional editing; (2) Cross-Modal Perception Guidance that aligns text and image features to separate transfer/preservation concepts; (3) a pipeline for generating 1024x1024 data pairs via region-specific makeup removal, establishing a unified benchmark.
AI.result: Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate improved regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across diverse styles, races, and poses.
AI.conclusion: MagicMakeup effectively addresses key limitations in makeup transfer through spatial constraints and concept disentanglement, offering a robust solution with high-resolution data generation and strong generalization capabilities.

title: Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention
summary: Streaming video diffusion models have made substantial progress toward interactive and dynamic world simulation, but the nested autoregressive and denoising loops of conventional next-frame generation hinder real-time deployment. Recent rolling-window methods pipeline denoising across multiple consecutive frames at different noise levels, improving throughput and long-horizon stability. However, they tokenize every state at the same fine spatial granularity, leaving substantial noise-dependent redundancy in the joint denoising window. We propose Ms.Forcing, an efficient streaming video generation paradigm that adapts spatial granularity to each state's noise level. Its Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier states, reducing the active-window token count by 45%, while Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches the density of visible non-sink keys and values to each query scale to further reduce attention cost. Because both schedules are fixed by window position, Ms.Forcing retains a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. We further introduce Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD), which assembles each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level, thereby reducing the mismatch between DMD training sequences and inference-time rollouts. The multi-scale design helps offset the additional training cost of backpropagating through overlapping windows. We include both quantitative and qualitative experiments to show that Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, while significantly improving VBench scores in both short video and long video generation setting.

AI.tldr: Ms.Forcing proposes a multi-scale spatial granularity approach for streaming video diffusion, adapting token resolution to noise levels, achieving 22.84 FPS on H200 (39.6% faster than baselines) with improved VBench scores.
AI.motivation: Streaming video diffusion models suffer from slow real-time deployment due to nested autoregressive and denoising loops in next-frame generation. Existing rolling-window methods improve throughput but tokenize all states at the same fine granularity, leaving noise-dependent redundancy.
AI.method: Ms.Forcing introduces (1) Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigning coarser patches to noisier states (45% token reduction), (2) Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matching key/value density to query scale, and (3) Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD) for better training-inference alignment.
AI.result: Achieves 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, with significant VBench improvements in both short and long video generation.
AI.conclusion: Multi-scale adaptation to noise levels effectively reduces redundancy in streaming video diffusion, enabling faster inference without sacrificing quality, while H-DMD improves training efficiency.

title: RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection
summary: In intelligent transportation systems, roadside 3D object detection provides wide-area perception crucial for traffic understanding, cooperative early warning, and safe autonomous driving. However, existing methods suffer from high sensitivity to camera extrinsics; even slight deviations (whether manifesting as transient jitter or persistent drift) can be significantly amplified by projective geometry. This cascade results in severe feature misalignment and degraded localization. To mitigate this limitation, we propose RECO, a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework that corrects extrinsics using piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets. RECO predicts a learnable range boundary to partition the scene into near and far regions, estimating region-specific pose corrections. A differentiable sigmoid gate then smoothly blends the two compensated geometries to preserve continuous BEV sampling and facilitate stable optimization. To supervise the refinement of extrinsics, we introduce an auxiliary reprojection loss that compares 2D bounding boxes projected from 3D ground truth against 2D annotations, optimizing it jointly with the standard detection objective. Extensive experiments on the DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under extrinsic perturbations demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across both yaw and $z$-axis deviations. RECO also generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent shifts, maintaining highly competitive performance under strict calibration uncertainty.

AI.tldr: RECO is a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework for roadside 3D object detection that corrects camera extrinsic perturbations by partitioning the scene into near/far regions with piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets, using a differentiable sigmoid gate for smooth BEV blending and an auxiliary reprojection loss for supervision.
AI.motivation: Existing roadside 3D detection methods are highly sensitive to camera extrinsic errors (jitter/drift), where even slight deviations cause severe feature misalignment and degraded localization due to projective geometry amplification.
AI.method: RECO uses learnable range boundaries to split scenes into near and far regions, applies piecewise 6-DoF pose corrections per region, blends them via a differentiable sigmoid gate for continuous BEV sampling, and trains with an auxiliary reprojection loss comparing projected 3D boxes to 2D annotations.
AI.result: RECO achieves consistent improvements over SOTA baselines on DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under both yaw and z-axis extrinsic perturbations, and generalizes well from transient jitter to persistent calibration shifts.
AI.conclusion: RECO effectively compensates for extrinsic perturbations in roadside 3D detection, showing robustness to both transient and persistent calibration errors while maintaining competitive performance under strict calibration uncertainty.

title: FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT
summary: Accurate segmentation of brain stroke lesions in non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans is critical for rapid clinical decision-making, yet remains difficult due to the low contrast between lesion and normal brain tissue, heterogeneous lesion morphology across ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes, and ambiguous boundaries caused by partial volume effects. Current deep learning approaches primarily optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, leading to imprecise delineation that can affect volumetric assessment and treatment planning. We propose FSB-Net, a frequency-spatial boundary network that leverages frequency-domain analysis for boundary-aware stroke lesion segmentation. FSB-Net introduces three components: (i) a Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) that applies the discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features, extracting high-frequency sub-bands as boundary representations; (ii) a Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) that performs bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for selective boundary enhancement; and (iii) a Spectral Boundary Loss that penalizes high-frequency discrepancies in the Fourier domain to optimize boundary sharpness. Built on a PVTv2-B2 encoder, FSB-Net is evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset containing both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases. Experimental results show that FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance in mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95.

AI.tldr: FSB-Net is a frequency-spatial boundary network that uses wavelet transforms, cross-attention, and spectral loss to improve stroke lesion segmentation in NCCT scans, outperforming U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+.
AI.motivation: Stroke lesion segmentation in NCCT is difficult due to low contrast, heterogeneous morphology, and ambiguous boundaries. Existing deep learning methods optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, leading to imprecise delineation affecting clinical decision-making.
AI.method: FSB-Net introduces three components: (1) Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) using discrete wavelet transform on multi-scale encoder features; (2) Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) for bidirectional attention between wavelet and spatial features; (3) Spectral Boundary Loss optimizing high-frequency Fourier discrepancies. Built on PVTv2-B2 encoder.
AI.result: Evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset with both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases. FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-domain boundary modeling significantly improves stroke lesion segmentation accuracy, particularly for boundary delineation in NCCT scans.

title: Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction in Dental CBCT using Fine-tuned Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
summary: Metal artifacts generated by dental implants significantly degrade cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) volumes, obscuring critical anatomical structures and compromising diagnostic precision. To address this, an unsupervised deep learning framework has been proposed for Metal Artifact Reduction (MAR) utilizing a Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) optimized for high-fidelity restoration. Unlike supervised methods that rely on unattainable voxel-aligned paired datasets, the proposed approach leverages an unpaired dataset of approximately 4,000 images, curated from the public ToothFairy dataset. The architecture integrates U-Net-based generators and PatchGAN discriminators, specifically tuned to mitigate generative hallucinations and preserve morphological integrity. Quantitative benchmarking on a held-out test set demonstrates a 34.6\% improvement in the Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) score, a substantial reduction in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) from 207.03 to 157.04, and a superior Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.9105. The framework achieves real-time efficiency with a 3.03 ms inference time per slice, effectively suppressing artifacts while preserving anatomical detail. Expert validation confirms high fidelity; however, to ensure reliability in extreme cases, the architecture is recommended as a clinical decision-support tool under human-in-the-loop oversight. By enhancing diagnostic clarity via a scalable software pipeline, this study provides a robust solution for high-fidelity dental implant imaging.

AI.tldr: An unsupervised CycleGAN-based framework for metal artifact reduction in dental CBCT imaging, trained on unpaired ~4,000 images from ToothFairy dataset, achieving BRISQUE improvement of 34.6%, FID reduction from 207.03 to 157.04, SSIM of 0.9105, and 3.03 ms inference time per slice.
AI.motivation: Metal artifacts from dental implants degrade CBCT volumes, obscuring anatomy and reducing diagnostic accuracy; supervised MAR methods are impractical due to the lack of voxel-aligned paired datasets.
AI.method: An unsupervised CycleGAN with U-Net-based generators and PatchGAN discriminators, trained on an unpaired dataset of ~4,000 images from the ToothFairy dataset, with tuning to reduce generative hallucinations and preserve morphology.
AI.result: 34.6% improvement in BRISQUE, FID reduction from 207.03 to 157.04, SSIM of 0.9105, and 3.03 ms inference time per slice; expert validation confirms high fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a robust, real-time, and scalable solution for dental implant MAR, recommended as a clinical decision-support tool under human-in-the-loop oversight for extreme cases.

title: Distribution-Alignment Bridge for Uncertainty-Aware Text-to-Video Retrieval
summary: This paper proposes the Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB), a framework that reconceptualizes text-to-video retrieval as a distribution alignment task rather than traditional deterministic point matching. By modeling both text and video embeddings as Gaussian distributions defined by mean and variance, DAB explicitly accounts for modality-specific uncertainty. We employ a deterministic, diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward their target video distributions through a truncated refinement process. This approach unifies probabilistic embedding and distributional transformation into a cohesive, end-to-end trainable system. To optimize cross-modal similarity, we introduce a distribution-aware contrastive loss based on Kullback-Leibler divergence. Extensive evaluations on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX benchmarks confirm that DAB significantly outperforms existing probabilistic and diffusion-based baselines, while providing calibrated uncertainty-aware ranking through bridge-induced distributional margins.

AI.tldr: DAB recasts text-to-video retrieval as distribution alignment using probabilistic embeddings and a diffusion-inspired bridge, outperforming baselines on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX.
AI.motivation: Traditional text-to-video retrieval uses deterministic point matching, ignoring modality-specific uncertainty. The authors aim to model and leverage this uncertainty for better cross-modal alignment.
AI.method: Models text and video as Gaussian distributions (mean+variance). Uses a deterministic diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward video distributions with truncated refinement. Trained end-to-end with a KL-divergence-based contrastive loss.
AI.result: Outperforms probabilistic and diffusion-based baselines on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX benchmarks. Provides calibrated uncertainty-aware ranking via bridge-induced distributional margins.
AI.conclusion: Probabilistic distribution alignment with a bridge-based refinement process is effective for text-to-video retrieval, improving both accuracy and uncertainty calibration.

title: HyWorldVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Hybrid World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models augmented with world modeling represent a promising paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving. While pixel-level future prediction enables fine-grained spatiotemporal reasoning, it compromises robustness in noisy driving scenarios. Conversely, latent-based world models alleviate this sensitivity but often incur limited interpretability and representational degradation due to absent pixel-level grounding. To reconcile this trade-off, we propose HyWorldVLA, a hybrid world-VLA framework that unifies pixel-level supervision and latent representation learning. In the pre-training stage, HyWorldVLA predicts video latents encoded by a pre-trained video VAE, while simultaneously reconstructing video frames to provide precise pixel-level grounding. During the subsequent co-fine-tuning phase, the model exclusively predicts latent features, which are fed into an action expert to generate trajectories. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks demonstrate that HyWorldVLA significantly outperforms both pixel-based and latent-based world model baselines. Notably, we present the first comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analysis of world model noise robustness in autonomous driving, establishing a new benchmark for evaluating future architectures.

AI.tldr: HyWorldVLA is a hybrid world-VLA framework for autonomous driving that combines pixel-level supervision (for grounding) with latent representation learning (for noise robustness), outperforming both pure pixel-based and latent-based world models on NAVSIM benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level future prediction enables fine-grained reasoning but lacks robustness in noisy driving scenarios, while latent-based world models are more robust but suffer from limited interpretability and representational degradation due to absent pixel-level grounding. The authors aim to reconcile this trade-off.
AI.method: HyWorldVLA has two stages: (1) Pre-training: predicts video latents encoded by a pre-trained video VAE while simultaneously reconstructing video frames for pixel-level grounding. (2) Co-fine-tuning: exclusively predicts latent features, fed into an action expert for trajectory generation.
AI.result: Outperforms both pixel-based and latent-based world model baselines significantly on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks. Also provides the first comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analysis of world model noise robustness in autonomous driving.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid approach effectively unifies pixel-level supervision and latent representation learning, establishing a new benchmark for evaluating noise robustness in future autonomous driving architectures.

title: Latent Variable-Mediated Cross-Learning for Few-Shot Acoustic Impedance Imaging
comment: The manuscript is currently under review
summary: Acoustic impedance imaging is a fundamental yet severely ill-posed problem in subsurface analysis: the seismic wavelet is unknown, observations are band-limited, and labeled well-log samples are extremely scarce (typically <1% of all traces). Existing semi-supervised deep learning methods mitigate few-shot problem by incorporating forward modeling, yet they either rely on inaccurate prior wavelet assumptions or introduce auxiliary networks, leading to unstable optimization and degraded performance. We propose RD-SCL, a novel framework that integrates regularized deconvolution with semi-supervised cross-learning. At its core lies a differentiable, closed-form first-order Tikhonov deconvolution operator that dynamically estimates the latent wavelet in the frequency domain during training, providing stable physics-guided feedback without explicit auxiliary networks and fixed wavelet priors. Building on this operator, we design a symmetric cross-learning that enforces consistency between predictions on labeled and unlabeled data, thereby effectively exploiting abundant unlabeled traces. Extensive experiments on the SEAM and Marmousi 2 benchmarks demonstrate that RD-SCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised methods, achieving substantial gains with lower computational cost. With only 56.5k learnable parameters and competitive runtime, RD-SCL offers a practical, physically consistent, and efficient solution for acoustic impedance imaging.

AI.tldr: RD-SCL integrates regularized deconvolution with semi-supervised cross-learning for acoustic impedance imaging, using a differentiable closed-form Tikhonov operator to dynamically estimate wavelets without fixed priors, outperforming SOTA methods with only 56.5k parameters.
AI.motivation: Acoustic impedance imaging is severely ill-posed due to unknown seismic wavelets, band-limited observations, and extreme scarcity of labeled well-log samples (<1% of traces). Existing semi-supervised methods rely on inaccurate prior wavelet assumptions or auxiliary networks, causing unstable optimization and degraded performance.
AI.method: RD-SCL introduces a differentiable closed-form first-order Tikhonov deconvolution operator that dynamically estimates the latent wavelet in the frequency domain during training. It then employs symmetric cross-learning to enforce consistency between predictions on labeled and unlabeled data, exploiting abundant unlabeled traces without fixed wavelet priors or auxiliary networks.
AI.result: On SEAM and Marmousi 2 benchmarks, RD-SCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised methods with substantial gains, lower computational cost, only 56.5k learnable parameters, and competitive runtime.
AI.conclusion: RD-SCL provides a practical, physically consistent, and efficient solution for acoustic impedance imaging, effectively addressing the few-shot learning problem through physics-guided feedback and semi-supervised consistency learning.

title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
summary: Large vision-language models are becoming increasingly dominant in 3D medical image interpretation, but we rarely know which internal units encode clinical findings or where that information lives in the representation. We first study this on a 3D chest vision-language model (Pillar-0) by probing its frozen vision embeddings. We show that (i) each radiological finding is encoded by a sparse set of ~10 vision-encoder channels that match full-feature classification performance and far exceed a zero-shot text prompting; (ii) turning off the channels tied to one finding, that finding's score collapses while unrelated labels stay stable; and (iii) the same sparse probe replicates on an architecturally unrelated 3D abdominal VLM (Merlin) suggesting a general property of frozen medical encoders. Our training-free concept channel probe (CCP) method, paired with a corpus-derived report template, outperforms published CT-CHAT on clinical efficacy and NLG metrics (F1 0.549 vs. 0.184; BLEU 0.483 vs. 0.373) at 22x lower latency.
